text: Horribly rude customer service. Didn't return our old tire after changing it. We had to go back again. Overcharged and fraudulently charged our credit card.

So I'll be the first to admit that I don't know anything about how to fix vehicles or how to gauge how much it should cost to repair a vehicle. So I have no idea if I got a good deal on my service. I do know that they had to replace a part on my car for a 2nd time that they replaced only 18 months ago. It cost $650.

So what really upset me and will keep me from going back there is that when I got into my vehicle I immediately felt that there was something wrong. I noticed that all my mirrors had been changed, my seat had been moved-not just forward or back, but it had been raise up, moved forward and the back support at been lowered, my steering wheel had been moved, my radio stations had been changed and all my AC controls had been changed. Then I realized that my car had 60-70 miles put on it. I had just filled up the tank only a few days before dropping my car off and I had a half a tank when I picked up my car only 2 days later (mind you I have only driven it maybe 15 - 20 miles on my 7 minute commute to work since filling it up.) 

I immediately called them and asked, "did you guys drive my car around?"
Steven replied "oh yes we take it out on two freeway test drives." I can understand and appreciate a couple of test drives and I would have over looked 20 miles or so put on my car. 
Then I asked "how far did you drive it 'cause I'm wondering why I dropped it off with a full tank of gas and its returned me to me with only half." 
He replies, "oh well sometimes we take them home with us." 
"I kind of wished that I would have known you took my car out for such a long commute. I don't think I would have come to you guys if I'd know that nor do I think I will be returning as a client." 
To which Steven replies, "oh uhh we should have reimbursed you for the gas, if you want to come back we'll give you $20." For which I did.

Its not so much the money really, its more that I feel violated in a way. Like I'm momma bear and someone had been sleeping in my bed. It was obvious to me as soon as I got into my car that someone had gotten REALLY comfortable in it and I had no idea what, where or with whom they were driving my car. It left me with a really bad taste in my mouth.

text:
I took my VW here based on a recommendation from a friend and after reading the other reviews on the site. The symptom was a noticeable "wobble" in the steering wheel - at low speeds the wheel traveled left to right and at high speeds it dampened out to a wheel vibration. The car tracked straight while on the road.

Steve diagnosed a worn tie rod, bad control arm bushings, and an unevenly worn front left tire. He replaced the tie rod, two control arms, put my full-sized spare on the left front, and the worn tire in the trunk, rotated the right side tires, did an alignment, and charged $600. I have no problems with any of this. He also told me I needed new tires as all four were very worn. I'd checked the day before and all four tires passed the penny test, so I told him to leave the tires on. He also showed me the bad parts.

When I got the car back I took the worn tire in the trunk and rolled it across some pavement. It rolled straight - no sign of uneven wear. I put it on the car's left rear wheel, then went to move the rear tire to the front to replace the spare but discovered 123 Auto had badly over-torqued all the lugs on the spare. Three of the five required penetrating oil to coax off, one came off with no lube but lots of extra persuasion, and I stripped the locking lug trying to get it off and had to have the lug removed by a tire shop I trust. Not good for a scenario where the spare gets a leak and I can't change a flat on the side of the road. The tire shop made no comment on the wear of my tires.

My car was also due for a 100k maintenance so I took it to my regular shop two weeks later. They found that the left front CV joint boot was torn and were puzzled as to why the prior shop hadn't replaced it when they'd done the tie rod and control arm work. My shop also said my tire wear was fine and treads were even on all four tires.

So, one star, because lots of little things make me not trust these guys, and I have places I can go that don't set off these alarm bells.

Update: After I posted this review, Steve called me to apologize for the issues with the lugs and for missing the CV boot issue. He was also extremely earnest about offering to show me why the tire he'd removed was bad, and offered to compensate me in cash for the work I'd had done elsewhere. I appreciate the call back, but declined to take him up on any of his offers.

text:
Some of the worse communication and customer service I've experienced. 

I called in on a Wednesday and made an appointment to bring in my vehicle on a Friday. I dropped off the vehicle for a diagnosis of the check engine light at 9a. I was told I would hear back by noon. 4p rolls around still nothing so I called back no answer. All good I know things get busy and hectic and car info gets lost in the shuffle sometimes. 

I hear back from someone at 430p and he tells me the issue - cool. He explains what parts I will need and I agree on the work that needs to be done. He tells me to return the vehicle on the following Wednesday to replace the part and so that their "electric guy" can re-program the vehicle. 

Wednesday I drop off the vehicle in the morning and they tell me it will be done by 12p. Great. 1p no call so I call and leave a message to get an update. Jim (the owner I assume) calls me back at 2p leaves a message saying they are still waiting for their electric guy and he will call me with an update. Not knowing if I should plan to find a ride home or if I should wait for the car to be done I called back at 430p and Jim is clearly upset that I called to get an update. After literally saying, "I'm returning your call to see if there was an update" he proceeds to be extremely rude over the phone and tells me "Did you not listen to my voicemail?" "there's no update!" What do you want me to tell you?! Are we done here? I said ok- thanks. Awkward. 

I actually was shocked that he would talk to a customer that way. Very unprofessional but hey maybe he was just having a day. I get it - but no need to raise your voice over the phone we are adults here. 

After that encounter I decided to stop calling the shop - that was on a Wednesday. 

4 days goes by - yes 4 days of not getting a call back or hearing anything from this shop so on the 5th day I decided to call. I asked for an update on the vehicle and the lady that works the front desk asked to call me back so she could "look into it." It turns out that that they were not able to fix my car and I needed to take it to the dealership. Not only was it a complete waste of time, but who knows when they would have called me about my car. The only reason I didn't rate it a one star is because they do free diagnostic and they didn't charge me for anything.

Very stressful not knowing what's going on with your vehicle, lack of consideration for customers who commute and need to make arrangements. Also after the temper tantrum it made it very uncomfortable to try to communicate with them. Seems very disorganized here, very messy shop, communication between staff members is an issue as well. 

10 total days passed by to be told they couldn't fix the issue.

Just take your car elsewhere for piece of mind and some professionalism.

So I did return and to no fanfare this time. What changed!

I brought my car in with the check engine light on--time to take a smog test, so that's no good.
I called ahead and was told to drop my car off later that week--no big deal, it was still running just fine.

Took my car in...and waited...and waited. 
No word back, so I called them to check in. I was told (by a mechanic who was very polite and nice, but couldn't provide any info) that they hadn't quite narrowed down the problem yet and that they would call me back later that day. 
I did get a call back--still not ready. I was told they would call me back the next day with details.
Fine, I can be patient, I don't use my car daily anyway. I can live with this.

Get a call the next day and am told:
"it will be $300 to fix"
me :"ok, $300 to fix what?"
mechanic: "There are 3 things wrong"
me: "what 3 things?"
mech: "well I wrote them down, but I don't have the list in front of me"
me: "could you go get the list?"
mech: "well there are 3 things wrong and they'll cost about $100 each to fix, so that's $300 total"
me: " well sure, but what are the problems exactly? What are you fixing?"
mech: "We found 3 problems and we'll fix them for $300, but you know you never know how much it costs until you get in there..."
me: "I'll be by to pick my car up this afternoon"

Sorry, but I'm not just handing you $300 and hoping for the best!

I picked up my car and took it elsewhere.

Turns out there was only 1 issue: got my car fixed and it definitely didn't cost $300.

text:
For about a month I seemed to have to press on my brake pedal a little harder each day to get my car to stop (and stay stopped). It felt like there was a balloon under my brake pedal and as I pressed on it, the balloon would deflate, causing my car to roll forward. Occasionally the car would lurch forward even with my foot firmly on the brake. 

So after reading all the positive reviews, I faithfully took my car to Emerald and spoke with Johnny (everyone's favorite employee-and he really was quite nice). Johnny told me they were quite busy, but that I could bring my car in that afternoon and they would get to it "as soon as possible". Which they did the next day. He told me that they had flushed the lines and checked all the connections, that my brakes seemed "soft", but I had 80% of my brake pads front and back so I should be fine. I asked "did you test drive it?" and was told that someone had indeed test driven the car. I had the sense they were very busy and not really willing to spend any more time and effort on my brakes. So, I paid $37 for the time they spent looking over the car and drove it off the lot. 

The problem persisted over the next month and got even worse, so I called Midas. The guy at the Geary street location (Jim) suggested that the car may have an issue with the master cylinder or power booster, but said I absolutely should not drive it, as it was very dangerous to do so. I said "I have been driving it like this for over a month". 

At the Midas shop the guys could not believe I had been driving the "death trap" for that long without an incident. They replaced all the lines, and replaced the master cylinder, they have to replace a seal in order for the car to be completely safe, and I have to wait to do that work because I am now broke, but at least the car stops now. 

So, bottom line is, although the guys may be nice, the shop is busy and they may or may not give your car the care and attention it (and you) needs.

text:
Looking at the number of stars some people give this shop, i find it SHOCKING.

I took my car here over a year ago for a simple oil change. The brakes were working well, and I had just had them checked out several months before by another shop that I had been using for many years. I came to pick up the car after the oil change, and one of the 2 owners said "by the way, your brakes are not working well...have you noticed that before?...no? well, i don't have time today but i'll look at it another time." I proceeded to drive the car away from the shop, and the brakes barely worked enough to stop the car. Thank you, Emerald Auto, for almost allowing me to drive off into a fatal car accident.

The shop then tried to repair the brakes and said that AFTER taking the whole car apart, they realized I had unusual molding on the brake lines and they couldn't find a part to replace them. This required the transfer of the car to the dealer, which wanted to charge me $2000 for fixing the brakes that were fine when I brought the car in for a change. Perhaps Emerald Auto needs to use a lighter foot when handling our cars, so as not to pound our brakes into the ground.

As an additional plus, it is fabulous that they have no space for anyone to put their car when they drop it off. Just an added bonus. Thank you Emerald Auto, as I am now the proud owner of a new Honda civic, which I will keep FAR from your shop when it needs a repair.

text:
I brought my car into Stress-Free Auto Care for a routine oil change and tire rotation. Instead, I was told I had an oil leak and that my front lower control arm bushings were torn and needed replacement. My car only had 37,000 miles on it, so I couldn't shake the feeling that I was being taken for a ride.

The inspection report flagged the bushing issue in red, which pressured me into agreeing to the repair. I ended up spending a staggering $2,580. This was my first time visiting this shop--I usually go to the Subaru dealership--and I deeply regret the decision.

Their claim of an oil leak was never confirmed. After some inspection, they said they'd need to remove more parts to investigate further. I declined. Then the receptionist acted like she was doing me a favor by charging me only half the inspection labor fee because they couldn't find the root cause. That felt manipulative.

A few months later, my car started having battery issues, so I took it to my dealership. I brought along the paperwork from Stress-Free for reference. The dealership replaced my battery and, upon inspecting the supposed oil leak, said it looked more like someone had splashed oil on the engine rather than an actual leak. When I asked about the bushing replacement, they said it was unusual for a car with only 37k miles to need that repair--though city driving could cause wear, it was hard to say definitively.

I also spoke with several male friends who are knowledgeable about cars. They all agreed that bushings typically don't need replacement until around 100k miles. That confirmed my suspicion: this shop may be taking advantage of customers, especially women, by recommending unnecessary repairs.

I'm angry and disappointed. I'll never take my car anywhere but the dealership again. What stings the most is that I told them I was looking for a neighborhood shop to build a long-term relationship with. Clearly, they didn't care. It was anything but "Stress-Free." Avoid this shop at all costs.

text:
This should have been a slam dunk five star rating. 

Great: My car died and was long overdue for a general check up including replacing the battery. Called around and Emerald was the only shop able to see me within a 48 hour period. Jim was able to get the car in mid-day that day and turn it around first thing in the morning next day. Really happy with the speed. A lot of people are concerned about the ethics of a mechanic - didn't get that vibe from Emerald at all. More of a "You want to come to us? Fine. You don't? Fine." The charges were reasonable and itemized.

Meh: Not much of a talker and handled my request while also handling another customer and the phone at the same time but as long as he gets the job done, that's all that counts.

Disappointing: Jim and team went 95% of the way (I hope) in doing the check up and replacing the battery. But the last 5% is where it was just simply sloppy. In the morning, I was dropped off at my finished car and the Emerald team had left the lights on all night - already significantly draining the brand new battery they had just installed in the car! Got in the car and the maintenance light was still on. I think they did do the work but didn't take the 30 seconds to reset the light. Similarly, the stereo panel was locked and required the "code" which is a fairly easy thing to punch in in any standard Honda. It did make me wonder about anything else that may have been hastily done. I called Jim to let him know about the things that were 95% there but missed out on the last 5% due to a lack of attention as I believe its much better to give direct feedback (I'd certainly prefer that in the business I run). I left a message but never got a call back. 

Overall, I would come to Jim again in a pinch but probably feel like I have to micromanage exactly what I wanted done and check it thoroughly to feel really comfortable.

text:
I pondered for quite a while whether this should be a 2-star review, but I could not agree with myself that Emerald Auto Repair deserves more than 1-star. This review has been posted after my first, and last ever, visit.

Wife took it upon herself to get an oil change (2013 Mazda 3) based on location and Yelp reviews, which led her to this place. Maybe that was my mistake for letting her do anything involving the maintenance of our automobile, but it's only an oil change, what could possibly go wrong? So I let her be and sent her with a note with the only instructions that she would need, which was to get 0W-20 oil, or 5W-20 if 0W-20 was too expensive. (Mazda owners manual kind of recommends either)

What the owners manual DOESN'T recommend is the oil that Emerald saw fit to offer and administer to the engine of our car. Apparently, wife was recommended a "blend", and not knowing what that is, she accepted that recommendation (because it was from someone who allegedly knows more about cars than we do). When she got home and gave me the invoice, I immediately knew that she didn't get what she was supposed to. The invoice says that she received a "blend" of "5W-30/10W-30/10W-40/20W-50." WTF is that?! 

Even the large text on the oil cap on my engine, which clearly says "SAE 0W-20", should have been a fairly major red flag to not continue with their 'recommendation.' 

This obviously seemed questionable, so I called as soon as I saw it, yet Jim, the guy who mans the phone and the front desk, insisted that we got 0W-20 and it was a perhaps a computer mishap. Well, there are numerous other things that tell me that was not a computer error: (1) the price that she paid did not reflect what a 0W-20 oil change would cost just about anywhere; (2) the decal placed inside the car window had a handwritten mileage for next oil change as +3,000 miles (Mazda recommended oil changes for these newer car engines is 5,000-7,500).

It was during this phone conversation that I learned that she had to bring the car back on Monday (it was Friday and they are not open on weekends) to get a part installed that they didn't do because it was not in stock. I didn't even think to ask what this was for, assuming it was connected with the oil change. I was already going to bring the car back on Monday and have them drain their garbage "blend" and put the proper oil in. 

On Monday morning, when I pressed, Jim admitted that we didn't get the oil that this car is supposed to receive, and so he got me in fairly quickly, and I left with my new (correct) oil and no additional charge. Before I left, though, I was asked to come back again for they still had the wrong part, which turned out to be an air filter. Not thinking about why am I getting a new air filter, I left. Unable to go back later in the day, the wife did... and came home with an additional $52 invoice. WHAT?! 

While I don't mind paying for the proper oil, this unnecessary air filter cost almost half of this new invoice. (I could have bought my own air filter online for half of what they charged me!)

I looked in the owners manual and I placed a call again. It recommends changing the air filter every 37,500 miles, of which my car has 15,000 miles less than that. Jim told me that the air filter was "dirty" and, probably seeing where I was going with my tone, said that they don't "upsell for things that aren't necessary". I am quite confident that my "dirty" air filter would have been good enough to last until its recommended time for change. I was offered my air filter back because "the trash wasn't picked up yet" but I declined the offer, because it's not like they are going refund this new one that we've already driven on (despite not many miles). 

Quite simply, this was a lot of hassle over one oil change... one oil change that should have been done correctly in one visit with zero additional phone calls. I would rather pay more at the over-priced dealership than go back to Emerald Auto Repair.

text:
This is a review I really never wanted to have to write.

In the past, I've sworn by Jim and his shop. I've referred other people to him. I've raved about him

That was then, this is now.

I don't know what changed; maybe it's because so many earlier satisfied customers, like myself, referred so much business that they got overwhelmed. I really don't know what happened here. But after today's experience, I'm finding another mechanic.

First off, I'm handicapped. I have multiple sclerosis. My car is 95% of how I get around; without it, I'm basically dead in the water.

I brought my 20-year-old Infiniti in because, increasingly, I was hearing a loud ominous squeaking that accelerated when the engine revs accelerated. I dropped the car off with a request to see what was causing it - being handicapped, I can't afford to be stranded somewhere - and also to please check the front brakes.

Verdict was a bad rear bushing. I said okay, fix that. He said I'd been right about the front brake pads needing to be replaced. Cool, do those too.

I was able to pick up the car a day later than he'd told me it would be done, with not one but THREE new bushings, and the new front brake pads we'd agreed on The bill was $750.

Right. Not happy, but I paid it. 

Guess what? Squeak was STILL THERE. In the interim, the driver's side door latch suddenly stopped working from the outside. I went back to Jim and said look, I can open this fine by leaning across the passenger seat but it would be nice to have access to my car without having to risk triggering the MS by long painful stretches, and oh by the way did you guys DRIVE this car before you said it was the bushings? Because the squeak is still there.

That was yesterday (Thursday), early. I let them know that I needed the car by this morning, since I had a noon appointment for medical stuff in Daly City. Last thing I heard was "I'll call you within the hour".

Five hours and two calls from me later, I was finally told "needs a new latch, about $237 out the door for the part, plus labor."

Upshot is, can't do it. Just blew $750 on three bushings for my still-squeaking 20 year old car. OK, he said, I'll put the door back on. You can get it tomorrow (Friday) morning.

Long story short: the car door now no longer opens from EITHER side. And managing to crawl across the front and start it, the air bag light came on and started flickering.

Oh, and turns out "I FINALLY drove the car and heard the squeak, it's a bad fan belt tensioner." Why not have driven it BEFORE we did five hundred plus bucks worth of bushings? 

When I asked him to please put the car door back the way it was when I drove it in so that I could actually use my car in the interim, I got first shouted out and then he turned his back and walked away.

It's a shame about this place. A year ago, I would have rated them as high as you can get. After today, time for a new mechanic. I wish them the best, Jim's a good guy, but I'm out of there.

Don't go here.

My left side brakes were grinding, no doubt they'll have to resurface the rotor. Checked Yelp, called Emerald, "Bring it in tomorrow morning."

Got there at 8:30/:45, said it would be $150 if it was just the pads. He said he'd call in two hours and let me know what it would be. Around noon I called to see what was up, "Can I call you back in 20 minutes?"... I called again "You're gonna need new rotors, so it'll be just over $300" "Both rotors?" "Yeah, they're under spec" "What time?" "Should be done by 4" 

At 4:30 I called again "Yeah it's ready, uh, hold on ... No it's not ready yet, can I call you back?" (are you starting to see a patter here?) 
At 5 I started to walk the distance from Willard street to the garage, all closed up with one guy just about to leave. "Hi..here for the Honda" He looked at me guiltily "Did he call you back?" "No, I just wanted to get here before you closed" He looks on a small board for my key and grabs the phone "The guy is here for the Honda, here talk to him"
"Hello? We close at 5:30 and you're car won't be ready until the morning" "I was told it would be done today and I need it tonight" "OK, do you have a spare key?" "??11 uh, yeah" "OK, go home and get it, your car's over on 9th, you can come over and pay in the morning." ...and hung up.

His buddy was looking mighty worried, still looking for my key. I raised an eyebrow, "Uh, that guy's mighty rude." He explained they were actually two different businesses, and that I should ask for some money off for my time and inconvenience. I took the N home, grabbed my key and took the N back. Drove home. He actually -did- change the rotors.

Don't go here.

text:
Subject: Formal Complaint Against Stress-Free Auto Care
Address: 2941 Geary Blvd, San Francisco, CA 94118

To Whom It May Concern,
I am writing to formally express my serious concerns about my experiences with Stress-Free Auto Care located at 2941 Geary Blvd, San Francisco, CA 94118- Phone: (415) 751-7860. Based on my multiple visits for repairs on two different vehicles, I feel compelled to warn other potential customers about the untrustworthy practices multiple misdiagnosis , and inflated charges at this establishment . 
Top Reasons to Avoid Stress-Free Auto Care:
1. Untrustworthy and Misleading Practices: I have experienced poor workmanship, misleading diagnoses, bogus additional fees and inspections having had the same issues addressed multiple times--specifically, vibration, leak, grinding noises, rough rotation, and shaky wheels when turning. Despite being told that these issues stemmed from the steering rack which they replaced , I am still facing the same problems after so many visits , which indicates either a lack of skill or intentional misdiagnosis to inflate charges. 
2. Alarming Payment Requests  Questionable Billing Practices 
One alarming aspect of my experience was the way I was treated when asked to pay a staggering amount of $7,651.01 in cash or cashier check!  It's unreasonable to expect customers to pay such a large sum in cash or by cashier's check, especially when all my credit card payments had been approved through the year. This request feels suspicious, suggesting they were aware that their previous repairs were inadequate. The ongoing issues--vibration, grinding noise, rough rotation, and shaky wheels--indicate that the problems were not resolved, and this pattern of misdiagnosis raises serious concerns about their shady business, expertise and integrity.
3. Inflated Fees and Bogus Charges: The shop has charged me excessively for repairs and introduced unjustified fees, including a "storage fee" of $175, which I was neither informed about nor signed for. This charge is not only unethical but potentially illegal.
4. Repeated Misdiagnoses and Concealed Issues: I brought my vehicle in for oil leak issues and a transmission inspection, only to be charged double fees for additional and unjustified inspections (over $900) for what should have been a straightforward assessment. They failed to inform me of the actual leak until I came to pay, after having the vehicle for ten days. Concealing this, despite the high inspection fees, is unethical and unacceptable.

My attempts to escalate the matter to his boss Mr. Yinon Weiss were met with indifference! 
I have documented all my interactions, including receipts and invoices, to support my claims. Given the pattern of behavior exhibited by Stress-Free Auto Care, I intend to file a complaint in court to protect other consumers from being subjected to similar experiences.

text: This is really a zero star review, but we all know that Yelp makes us give one star. I was recently in San Francisco, and had car trouble on the drive down. text:
This incident took place in 6/2016. I didn't follow up on Yelp at the time, but recently thought, "I use Yelp, so I should contribute information."

I had brought our BMW 325xi to Metric a couple times prior, once limping in with a bent belt pulley, another for LOF and brake fluid flush. The first visit was very satisfactory and avoided serious damage. The second visit went OK, but they forgot to reset the CBS (condition) codes; I noticed all the warnings from before the service were still on before I left, so brought their tech back out to reset them; a minor annoyance.

I stopped going to Metric after I brought the car back for newly-balky power windows and door locks. It turned out the battery was shot, so we scheduled a replacement. They performed the work, I picked up the car & paid, and went for a drive to Half Moon Bay. On the way, the dash display started throwing messages about faults in the AWD, while the car alternately surged and lagged at ~60mph. I pulled into a parking lot at the earliest opportunity, where I proceeded to wait 3 hours for a tow truck, as the car refused to start once turned off. I called back Metric to let them know of this new severe failure. AAA towed the car back to Metric, where I learned the next day the technician had failed to secure all connections to the battery terminals! I wasted 3 hours and risked severe damage to the car because Metric failed to install a battery properly, one of the simplest maintenance tasks on a car. The car has shown none of these symptoms since this was resolved.

To their credit, Metric took my call, paid my ride home and back to pick up the car, and refunded the full cost of the invoice. They're nice guys, pleasant to work and talk cars with, but that should never lead to such gross inattention to detail. Seeing the recent good reviews, perhaps they've upped their game since.

text:
In all fairness, the staff was very friendly and efficient - they were able to get parts and replace the clutch and flywheel on my Boxster in only 2 days.

HOWEVER...

I bought my car under unusual circumstances (the previous owner had brought it into the shop before deciding to sell). When I bought the car, I was told that the clutch would need to be removed and disassembled in order to determine what was wrong with it. I was also was warned that the flywheel (which is $1200 for the part alone) could possibly also need replacement but that we would only know once the clutch was removed. No problem. The shop tech, Andy, even advised me that we could install a solid or lightweight flywheel instead of the expensive and problematic OEM Porsche DMFW for a significant cost savings. Sounds like they were looking out for my best interests!

But then I got the call from Rob, the shop manager, who told me that both the clutch and flywheel were bad (as well as a few assorted other items) and needed replacement to the tune of an additional $1400. I told Rob what Andy had told me about installing an alternative flywheel, and Rob insisted that he was wrong and that I had no options but to install the $1200 flywheel from Porsche. Out of curiosity, I checked online and found that the part lists for $700-800 on average. I even called another Porsche-specialized shop down the street from Metric, and they quoted me $900 (including their markup!). Now, I understand that mark-ups are how shops stay in business, and I am all for paying talented people to do good work, but $500 in pure profit on ONE part? After bringing up these concerns Metric was only willing to knock $50 off the "list" price they planned on charging me. 

Feeling backed into a corner and knowing I would have to re-pay another shop for the labor to re-do the job with the cheaper part, I reluctantly allowed them to finish. $3100 for a clutch rebuild and new flywheel... OUCH.

On top of all this, the previous owner of my car told me that Metric Motors has serviced it since the day its factory warranty expired. I asked Rob for a list of recent services that had been performed and he told me that this was the first time that this car had been in their shop. After the service was complete, I went home and dug through the paperwork the previous owner had given me...and found 20+ service records from Metric! First time in the shop...Seriously?

I wouldn't exactly say Metric had my back as other Yelpers have experienced.

I went to this shop because it is right by my apartment and the reviews seemed overall favorable. I needed my wiper motor replaced, a new battery and other general maintenance. I convinced him to just take a look and as soon as he saw it, he essentially cussed under his breath and said something about how hard it is to find good mechanics in the city and said he'd call me on Monday to schedule a time to replace it.

He irritatedly told me some sob story about how he talked to the owner and they think the crack was already there and they are a small shop blah blah blah and weren't going to replace it. I was completely flabbergasted! I am NOT the kind of person to lie about something like that and if you'd seen the cracks they so clearly came from the work they did. replies:
[{'id': 'D0C34Ihmbl0YghEbz8g37A', 'text': 'For many years our family business has been known for its high quality service and having our customers' best interest in mind. Unfortunately, there was a misunderstanding in this case.

When we inspected the wiper motor it became clear that copious amounts of leaves had fallen into the drainage areas and had flooded the windshield motor. If the drainage area is poorly maintained then the motor will eventually burn out. Being that this part had to be replaced, our shop looked up the cost from the dealer, which came out to be around $500. Realizing that this was an exorbitant amount, we explained to our customer that she might be able to find the part cheaper online. We allowed her to keep her car in our shop till she found the part herself, even at our own expense of time. Generally the price of leaving your car in our shop is $85 daily, but we were trying to give this customer a hand and let her keep her car in our shop charge free. We feel we tried to do our customer a good deed.

As the owner of Hayes Auto Repair, I am not into selling parts, although selling parts has become the standard of marketing in the automotive industry for many shops. We tell our customers the options available to them and let them decide which path they would be willing to take. Whether it is buying a part online or purchasing it from the dealer directly - which is inherently more reliable - we let our customers make that decision.

In this situation it is important to understand this analogy. You can buy a steak at a restaurant for $5 or you could buy a steak at another restaurant for $15. Are they the same? Of course not. We try to give our customers the best quality service along with access to the best parts available, but we still allow the option of installing a part of lesser quality if so desired. 

In regard to the 8" cracks the customer claims to have come from our work, it is clear to us that she did not fully understand the extent of our work when making this accusation. The work involving the wiper motor has nothing to do with the windshield glass at all. You do not even touch the window for this job. 

Hayes Auto Repair has been a family business for over 50 years, giving honest and high quality work to the community. Our business is known for keeping our customers best interest in mind and going out of our way to help, which has given us our good reputation throughout the Bay Area. We extend our hands out to our customers guiding them through the confusing process of automobile maintenance and reparation - helping them and their cars for the future.', 'author': {'id': '-5nErriWQCpzHq6QuKp_0Q', 'url': 'https://www.yelp.com/user_details?userid=-5nErriWQCpzHq6QuKp_0Q', 'name': 'Alan Y.', 'photo': 'https://s3-media0.fl.yelpcdn.com/buphoto/uYQjruWM4OeM94QSMKoojA/90s.jpg'}, 'timestamp': '2011-09-29 21:54:56'}]

The next day they said the car was finished but they were only able to install the brake actuator and not the pump. text:
ROBBED BY A TECH

I came here for an oil change based on the overwhelmingly positive reviews here on yelp. I am a delivery driver and receive a fair amount of direct tips in cash. This cash often finds it's way into my center console during a shift, and sometimes gets left overnight. 

The day I had my oil changed here I'd had around 80-100 dollars in my center console, including a crispy 50$ and even a 2$ bill. Having sort of forgotten about it, I didn't think anything of it until the next day when I was going to clean out the center console after my shift. The money was gone.

Having dealt with theft repeatedly since moving to SF I was beside myself. I couldn't believe this had happened again. My cars have been broken into several times and one was even stolen in the last year from in front of my house. This, however, did not have the feel of a break-in. Nothing was rummaged through or strewn about and everything was in its place, except for the money in the center console. I started going through things in my head, thinking about who I'd had in my car, trying to figure out an explanation for this, when suddenly I remembered the oil change. 

There is simply no other explanation for the disappearance of this money. Upon speaking to the manager I was dismissed and told that none of his guys are thieves, and although he "doesn't give a fuck about one hundred dollars" we were unable to come to an equitable solution. 

I kept putting off sharing this but wanted to warn others of the way I was treated here. I will never return to this place for any reason.

I go to pick up the car and the receipt totalled more than the order form I signed. I spoke with a manager and he said that he sent me an e-mail quote via Yelp and that it had the higher amount. I did not read my emails that day. He expected me to pay the higher quoted price. I wasn't born yesterday. I paid what I signed off on and nothing more.
On top of all this the guy told me I needed new brake pads up front but failed to notice that a caliper pin bolt had broken off and the inside of the wheel rim was rubbing on the caliper and almost fell off. Had I not noticed this when I was changing the brake pads myself, it could have been a catastrophic brake failure, and with SF hills someone could have gotten killed (this van weighs 9,000lbs!). What sort of mechanic sees that pads are worn down 90% but fails to notice huge scratches on the caliper and a broken caliper pin bolt?!? (See picture). This place aught to be shut down. Don't risk your life or your that of your family's. Go somewhere reputable or get a referral from friend/co-worker. Whatever you do, DO NOT let these people near your car.

And obviously they weren't making any money out of this case. But the worst thing was, when we got there, the car was parked in a street parking non tow away space. They wanted us to move the car so they can park another car in the public parking space. They wouldn't give us our car keys to get it towed until we demanded it because they wanted to position their car for the space. We have other cars and friends, so we will be giving the business to someone else and telling our friends of this experience. But maybe they don't care about our business since they have so many people bringing their cars to them?

This place rubbed me the wrong way. Maybe it was just my experience. I brought my car in for a oil change and saw that they had good reviews and the appointment making process seemed easy. I can pretty much get next day appointments. I had a check engine light also so I wanted them to take a look at it for my second visit. So in total I probably made about 3 visits. 

My first oil change went smoothly without a hitch. The total was like $39 bucks which made me super excited to go back to them because normally I pay about $70 since my car "supposedly" only takes synthetic oil. So you can only imagine how stoked I was to get a oil change for almost half the price. 

Then I came back a second time and this time I also had a check engine light on (I don't think this had to do with their oil change but just coincidental). So I decided to have them give me an oil change and to check my engine light since they do diagnostics for free. When I got my car back they said something was wrong with my electrical something something I don't really know and that I had to make a weekday appointment to get that fixed so I was like okay fine. I went and paid for my oil change and made a comment with the cashier lady that it's awesome that they charge so little for a synthetic oil change and she was like "you didn't get synthetic oil, it was just a regular oil change." I didn't know what to say at that moment. I was thinking don't they usually check based on your car and etc and etc to determine what type of oil to use. So then she asked a mechanic to come over to speak with me because I wasn't sure how this will affect my car since I have always been using synthetic. HE DIDN'T KNOW THE ANSWER TO MY CONCERN! I was shocked since I am used to oil change stations telling me that my car needs synthetic oil (I've been to a few such as Pep Boys, Jiffy Lube, and Sunset Service). The mechanic offer me know reassurance that the fact he put regular oil vs synthetic oil to my car would be okay. And he returned the question by asking me "oh your car takes synthetic oil?" Well I guess my fault for assuming that they would know this better than me. But stupid me already made an appointment for them to check my check engine light issue so I came back a third time. I brought it back to them the next day and they fixed it which cost me about $370. The light came back a few days later but will go off and then came back again. 

Lesson learned. I just went back to my regular mechanic and oil change station even though their hours weren't as convenient. They fixed it and I never saw the light again and I'm back to my $70 oil change. Sunset 76 you can stop emailing me reminders...

text:
Dear. Mr. Louis Bateh,

I've been here several times before without a problem, but this time I was really disappointed. I think the recent good yelp reviews have caused Sunset 76 repair to get busy and not need us regular customers anymore because I have to now make an appointment 1 week in the future to get repaired. How am I supposed to know when my car breaks down? Also the website is super difficult to find out how to make an appointment. I've never been able to figure it out. They won't make one for me when I'm there in person and that sucks. I can go to the Honda Service Center on 9th and Irving and either call or do it online easily so that's where I'll be going. 

First Repair: I came here about a month ago for my battery. They checked it out and told me it just had a low charge and charged me $25. I had also asked them to check the radio that wasn't working and they said it was a bad wiring and they couldn't fix that. OK. A few days later, my car battery dies again. Well, I don't have the money or time because I'm getting my Master's degree in Nursing on Monday and have a lot of finals/projects/papers to do so I've been getting around on bus and with my husband's car (luckily he works for Google and the shuttle picks him up close by). So because the problem didn't get resolved the first time, I had to come back at some point. My car has been in the garage for a few weeks until I can got a chance to take it in. That day was today.

My battery had died so my husband jumped it for me. And guess what? The radio magically worked again! Sunset 76 told me it was bad wiring so I guess they were wrong not just about the battery but also the radio. Since it doesn't restart without a jump, I needed it to get checked out since they are just a few blocks away from me and have always accommodated me and I figured just a simple repair like a new batter (I would have happily purchased the parts or called AAA to do their battery service for me. I showed up at 7:15 AM, park my car in an open space, and turn it off because I assume they've always helped me and what else would I have known to do? You don't walk away from a running car! I come up to the window and let the guy know my car needs to be checked and he tells me that he can't today because they are booked. So I ask for tomorrow and he says I need to make an appointment for next week because they are sooo busy. I asked how do I do that. He tells me to go on the website and doesn't even give me a card, I had to ask for one. I said that my car was parked on the lot and won't re-start and he starts yelling at me telling me I shouldn't have done that. How was I supposed to know? I've done that about the last half a dozen times I've been there with my 2 cars. So he tells me he can have it towed. Well, I have no choice but to take my business elsewhere at this point. So I called AAA to tow it to the Honda Center on 9th and Irving since Sunset 76 obviously doesn't need my business and doesn't care to be polite to their regular customers. I think from now on I'll just get my oil changes at the Honda Center and not have to deal with rude mechanics.

text:
Quite simply, this shop's Yelp rating is misleading. These guys do sloppy work with nonexistent customer service. I would recommend going anywhere else and I will not be returning.

I went to this place two weeks ago. I opted not to goto my usual shop (San Bruno) as I felt it was convenient to try a place in the Sunset. I just needed to have a new set of tires mounted and balanced. Easy enough right?

I was told it would be an hour and a half. Two and a half hours later I picked up my car. I was told my total was $100. When asked about using their Yelp deal the cashier coldly stated, "...uh... You could... But... Uh... We don't make much money on the tire jobs. Your total is $100," WTF? 

ON TO THEIR SLOPPY WORK: Later that night I had an odd feeling something was off. I checked my tire pressure and found the following:

Tire 1: 40.9
Tire 2: 40.0
Tire 3: 39.0
Tire 4: 34.0 (the guy also did not put the valve cover back on either, THANKS!)

Yes, I checked these values two more times with another gauge and received the same results. What the hell happened?

Mind you, these are stock OEM wheels which are recommended to have a pressure of 30.0 to 32.0 psi give or take one a psi. Overinflation makes your tires more prone to a flat or an accident, causes a rough ride, and at the very least can lead to expedited wear on your tires.

This shop either had no idea what they were doing, were in a rush, simply didn't care, or all of the above. It's inexcusable. I would be terrified to let these guys touch my car again and would recommend against letting these guys touch your engine.

I was referred to these guys multiple times by neighbors and friends but unfortunately I was unable to get my problem solved with my car even after bringing it back in.

I have an old high mile Toyota, it has a few things wrong with it, birfield joint noises, oil leaks, dangerous low oil pressure, spark plugs etc. I got a quote and it was above what I had saved to fix my car so i left out the recommended belt replacements and the suspension work on the Birfield(CV joint) because of their recommendations and the belts looked okay and the suspension stuff was not crucial more just annoying and loud when turning left.

The engine and low oil pressure was my biggest concern, at low rpm's and after driving for 15 minutes it drops and will cut off-they found 2 oil leaks(I only knew of one), one on the head and one underneath. I paid 1k for them to drain my oil supposivley fix the leaks and change my spark plugs. after a week of getting it back the second time and them reassuring me there were no longer any leaks, which was impossible because I could see new drips on the ground. I thought hey these guys are nice why would they lie, it's probably residual oil left over from dripping down so I brought it into my garage with cardboard and now it's been 3 weeks and still drips every night-I basically just paid 1k for my spark plugs replaced and my oil drained and new 10w40oil replaced.

So I do not think these guys are bad guys? No, maybe just not the best mechanics with my type of car or they were having an off 3 weeks while dealing with my car? I do not really know because they seemed really busy and people have recommended them so they must do some work really well and have fair prices for others. I know one of the brothers was out for a bit, but I think if you have an engine issue or need to diagnostic work trouble shooting to figure out your repair it may make sense to bring it somewhere else. Still super nice guys but I keep having to tell myself it was another learning experience so I don't cry after working hard to save the money for the repair.

I wanted to like these guys, because they do seem honest, and their prices are reasonable.

About a year and half ago, I had my brakes done on my 2011 Mustang. Afterward, I heard a squeal at high speed and a chirp when going over bumps. I assumed it was brake dust, but it didn't go away. I took the car back after a few months, but they said everything was fine.

I just had to replace the rear brakes, because the drivers side inner pad was almost at metal-to-metal. The new brake shop showed me that there are pins on the back of the inboard rear brake pad (the one with the wear indicator tab) that sit in the slots, and if the slot doesn't line up with the pins, the inside pad will not sit properly and WILL cause a severly uneven wear of the pad... and will likely cause one side of the steel backing plate to contact the rotor in short time.

Which is what happened. Which is what seems to have been causing the noises. Which, even with me buying the parts myself, just cost me 300 bucks.

Aligning the pins on a brake pad seems pretty basic for a brake shop. Sorry guys.

text: This shop has glowing reviews and I was excited to see such a highly recommended auto repair business within walking distance of my home which is perfect for me because that meant I could drop it off, work from home for the day and walk over when it was done to pick it up. I've also been looking for "my" mechanic for a while. Someone I can trust to do repairs that are needed and not try to cheat me. I took my car here no less than 6 times. A couple of examples - my car was making a creaking noise, took it to Simon and he said the axel needed to be replaced (can't remember if it was the left or right side) but he replaced it. Well the minute I backed it out and drove half way down the street I noticed it was still making the same noise. So I took it back and he checked it out, turns out the other side needed to be replaced as well. I would think a mechanic would check both sides...? But, I had him repair it and it was fine, but the lack of care concerned me. Another time I asked if he could check my transmission, just as a precaution. Well he had me park my car across the street, and mind you, I live a few blocks away, but I had a clear view of my car from my kitchen window. The car never moved, and was in the exact same position when I picked it up, so I'm wondering when he did the inspection... I was charged of course...The last time I had him do a repair he did my front brakes. He said I just needed pads and he did the work. The next week I took a trip up the coast and my car started making a horrible noise. I had my brakes checked and repaired before I left right, it couldn't be them. I ended up finding a random gas station and paid the guy $50 to grease them which helped with the noise a bit, but it came back. Really put a damper on the trip because we were worried the car was going to fall apart and we'd be stranded. Once I made it back I called Simon and he "didn't have time" that week, so I made an appointment for the following week. Seems like he would at least try to squeeze me in since he had just worked on my car and I had a concern about the work done. The following week he took a look and said nothing was wrong. I ended up taking my car to multiple places and finally the dealer who said I needed a new brake job and rotors. I had to pay for the diagnostic of course, and I thought they were trying to cheat me because I'd just had my brakes done and elected to not let them do any work on my car. Finally took it to another local shop to a man who has done repairs for me in the past. I should've stuck with him, but I switched to Glenview Automotive because the shop was closer. He inspected my car and immediately saw I needed rotors, and now new pads because the pads Simon put on were installed on bad rotors. My car drove perfectly after that. I'm not sure why my experience was so different than other reviews, but it's very disappointing. Maybe he just didn't like me personally, but the lack of care showed in his work. I don't need a fancy shop or a bff, just a trustworthy mechanic, especially as a woman. Despite me going to him for work multiple times, I thought it was interesting how when I would call for appointments he would say he was too busy, maybe he was hoping I'd get the hint and stop bringing my car to him. Well, the hint has finally been received.

text:
TL;DR - Took my truck in for a general inspection and valve clearance check. Was told they didn't know how to do the valves and argued with me about what engine I have. Had general inspection done, needed a new rack and pinion. Was charged 2x the cost for the rack compared to other sources. Power steering went out immediately afterwards. Took truck back and they said they couldn't find a problem, power steering goes out again almost immediately. Never taking truck there again. Too much time wasted. 

---------------------------------------------

So far I'm not particularly impressed, though I'll give them a call tomorrow and see if they can help resolve the problems they have left me with. 

I took the vehicle to 1701 Auto Care with the intention of having my valve clearances checked, the truck being a 2000 Tacoma Prerunner (Gen1 Tacoma). It is the 2.7 liter I4 3RZ-FE engine, running shims for valve clearances. Upon getting to the shop the owner informed me that I in fact had hydraulic lifters and didn't need valve adjustments. I told him I didn't think that was true, but if he could double check I needed to get to work. I also asked him to give the truck a quick once over, since I hadn't had the time to care for it between work hours and other responsibilities. 

After confirming that I do not have hydraulic lifters, because I have a Gen1 Tacoma I called to again ask the owner to double check and then perform the valve clearance inspection. He told me he was not comfortable then said something about it making sense on Honda's but not my truck. text:
I recently took my wife's car to Car Care Service and spoke with Wayne, the owner of the business. I requested the following basic work:

Change engine oil and filter
Change gear box oil
Change spark plugs
Change engine air filter
Change cabin air filter
Flush and refill engine coolant

The problems began after my wife picked the car up. When I took a quick look at the final bill and the car, I noticed that a) I was charged more than the original estimate and b) the car was missing a front wheel cover.

The following morning I drove back to Car Care Service to ask Wayne a) why the bill was higher and b) where the wheel cover might be. As I was talking to him his mechanic came walking out of the shop with the missing wheel cover. Wayne then explained that the bill was higher due to his supply house providing an expensive carbon activated cabin filter that cost $61.50, rather than the original estimate of about $30.00. 

When I got home from work that night I began a more thorough inspection of the work and the following day I contacted other local repair shops to assess what they would charge for similar work.

First, the work inspection: 

1) I pulled off the cover of the cabin filter (which filters the air before it blows through your air vents) and was shocked in two ways: First, I found the compartment absolutely full of leaves and dirt! While everyone knows that the cabin filter compartment should be cleaned out and wiped down when replacing the filter, the mechanic at Car Care Service chose to simply pull out the old filter and slap in a new one amidst all of the leaves and dirt that had been blown in there. My second shock was when I found it was not a carbon activated filter, as Wayne had told me, but cheaper micro-fiber paper filter.

2) Soon after, an engine warning light came on indicating that the engine coolant that mechanic had changed was low. I had to then pick up engine coolant and top off the reservoir to the minimum level required.

Second, the cost of parts and service:

1) The cabin filter: Car Care Service acquired the cabin filter from a wholesale supplier named WorldPac. While $61.50 may be the "list" price of the WorldPac part, I asked another local repair shop to contact WorldPac and request a price for the same part. After calling WorldPac they told me that that exact same filter would cost them about $18.00 wholesale and they would typically mark it up about 30% or so to a retail price for the customer. A 30% increase over $18 is just under $24. With these numbers in mind, Car Care Service chose to mark up the cheaper paper filter well over 300%!

Relative to being overcharged for the filter, I then decided to obtain estimates for the entire list of maintenance service items that I set forth above. What I found from my research is that it looks like I was charged overall about $200 more by Car Care Service than I would have paid at another repair shop in Alameda.

Note that I didn't just write this review before presenting my concerns to Wayne. I initiated my contact with him via email. In one of his emails he finally admitted that in installed a "microfiber filter" (aka cheaper paper filter).

When I expressed to Wayne, via email, my concerns regarding the sloppy, unacceptable work and being overcharged for the cabin filter, among other things, his response was:

"I am not responding to this e-mail. Call me personally if you would like to discuss this.
Wayne"

So I called him. I left a message with someone else in the shop and she told me he would call me back within a few days (I also asked her if I could speak with the mechanic who worked on my wife's car directly and she said it was their policy not to let their mechanics speak to customers). After a few days, when I hadn't heard from Wayne, I called him again. This time I got him on the phone.

The essence of what he told me was:

a) He had talked to the mechanic about his sloppy work.
b) All of the prices he charged me are fair.
c) Since I make a decent income (his assumption without knowing my income or expenses) I shouldn't be complaining, as he is just trying to make a living.

Not once during the conversation did I hear him offer an apology for his mechanic's sloppy work and the extra time I had to spend to fix things. Nor did I hear him offer to make it up to me in some way. He simply defended everything.

In the end, soon after my disappointment and frustration with Car Care Service I found another garage in Alameda where I consider the service to be excellent and at a fair price. It's called Alameda Auto Care, on Eagle Avenue, near the corner of Park St. (just a few blocks down from Car Care Service), run by Andy and David.

The end result, I'm sorry to say, is that I will never again take my cars to Car Care Service. I cannot recommend them. I'm taking my cars to Alameda Auto Care.

This is a review that went from 5 stars to 1 star in a matter of ten long, abusive minutes. PLEASE NOTE!!!

I took my car to Xiao at Car Care Service in July. He was fantastic! He worked with me to find cheaper parts and did excellent work on my car in a timely manner. He even topped off my fluids free of charge. Really, I thought I'd finally found my car repair guy. 

At the time of that first visit in July our Sienna (2000) was making a very loud noise every time we ran the AC. Xiao diagnosed the problem as being the auxiliary fan. When I picked up the car he mentioned that there might be some initial rubbing noise, but that it would wear off. No problem. Well, fast forward to October and the car still makes the exact same sound when I run the AC. I finally took it in today to ask him about it. 

I had no intention of asking for free work nor did I feel as though he had misdiagnosed the car initially. Our car is super old and has multiple problems. I expected back in July that there would probably be more than one problem going on. Nevertheless, the sound was the exact same and still needed to be addressed. I figured he could help me out again. 

At the very mention that we were still hearing the same sound -- literally it was close to the first sentence I spoke to the man -- he began hollering at me in a very defensive tone. I questioned him about why he was feeling defensive, trying to reassure him that I wasn't accusing him of misdiagnosing the problem, but just trying to explain to him what was going on so he could help me. To no avail. He quite literally just had a psychotic break in front of me. Ten minutes of yelling about how "90% of the people in this country are stupid and wouldn't understand if I tried to explain to them." 

Trying really hard to remain calm b/c he was getting so out of control, I reminded him that I wasn't accusing him of doing something wrong and I was in his shop because I was looking for his help. Again, to no avail. He said he didn't care about loosing customers or making money or about being nice to people. He said he had basically had it with people and he was going to say whatever he wanted, even if it was mean and rough. He quite literally went off on me as though I represented the entire American population that has apparently wronged him. 

After yelling at me for 10 minutes, he walked away and began making tons of noise. Not sure if he was throwing stuff around or just hitting things, but it was getting very weird. I mentioned to the other man working there that Xiao needed some help to calm down and get a grip. He apologized to me very quietly a number of times. 

Xiao knows quite a bit about cars. He is very capable. He has also just hit some sort of wall mentally. BE VERY CAREFUL!!! I felt very unsafe in his presence today.

text:
Okay, so based on most the previous reviews, I thought this place seemed better than most shops in the area. I was a little skeptical though as I read several other reviewers that said these guys didn't know what they were doing and were just okay mechanics at figuring problems out. Trust me when I say you will want to read this review on how I wasn't helped by them at all. 

So yesterday I was driving my VW Passat and I was going about 40 mph and my car just shut off while driving. It was so quiet that I didn't even know it shut off and it was coasting to a stop. I turned the key and it started right back up. I'm not a mechanic but this tells me a lot of key information on how to figure out what is wrong with it. First off, it coasting the way it did, instead of jerking to a stop, would seem more electrical or possibly spark plugs and not like any fuel or fuel pump problem. The same goes with it starting right up, as it wouldn't have a perfect start if it were sucking fuel back up first. I have mechanic buddies and this is first day stuff.

But I called Alameda Import Automotive and explained all of this and right afterward, do you know what their mechanic told me? "I will have to take it home with me and drive it around for a while until it shuts off to figure out how it is acting and what it is doing."

I said, "I just explained exactly what it was doing so what would you need to do that for? How would you seeing it do exactly what I just explained happened help any more besides just wasting a bunch of time?" 

I had to explain what happened again and he said, "sounds like a fun one," meaning it seemed like it would be a hard thing for him to figure out, if ever. Are you kidding me? This is easy for a good mechanic to figure out. Check the spark plugs, check any electrical that could possibly effect the whole car, do some work which you would be paid to do. One of my friend mechanics who lives out of state told me many great steps he would take to figure it out very quickly, without ever needing to see it shut off while driving it. He had a wealth of knowledge, whereas the mechanic I spoke to here didn't give any idea as to what he thought was going on, and didn't seem to have a clue, but instead he said it seemed like a fun one and said he would have to take it home with him to figure it out. If you want a mechanic that will actually listen to you on what went wrong with your car when something went wrong, this is not the place. At least the guy I spoke with. Pathetic. 

So they can read this review and apologize and try to explain themselves like they do toward every negative review, but that simply doesn't change the fact that their mechanic was clueless and didn't seem to care at all. Maybe the owner/manager is better and actually tries, that's why he responds to every negative post. But check your staff pal. I just told the facts, what else is there to know?

text: I went to this place to find out the source of a noise coming from the front right side of my 2003 Honda Accord. I had a feeling it was coming from the wheel. It was not the car brake pads because it is not associated with me pressing the brake. I constantly hear it when I drive. It does not increase when I turn left or right. So, I went to this shop because it was 15 mins walking from home. I arrived 9:00AM. I gave them the car. They told me it will take an hour to find out what is going on and they will call me. They did not call. I called them at 10:30 AM. They told me that they did not have chance to diagnose the car. After 30mins, he called me saying that he can not diagnose the car because the car is low on oil and he need to change oil or add to it before he can start. I told him that I just changed the oil from another shop and I would like to go back to them because they will add oil for free. The car did not have oil issue and I was coming to fix the noise not the oil. I know that my car burn oil and this is not my issue now. He refuse to do anything unless I change or add oil. So, I agree that he add oil. After 2 hours he called me back and told me that the problem is the transmission. The sound is coming from the transmission and do not know how to fix it. I need to come to the shop and take the car to transmission spaciest. I did not believe him because the car go from 1 to 2 to 3 to 4 smoothly. However, he made me feel so bad. If he is true, then I need to buy a new car. I did not have to go to the mechanic for few days because I have a lot of work. He make me always thinking about the issue and always stressed specially while driving the car and hearing the sound. I was about to buy another car because the cost is not worth trying to fix the car. After few days I took the car to another mechanic. He drove the car in 10mins. He said that he does not think it is the transmission. In one hour, he told me that the problem was bad axle and he fixed it with 150$.

text:
This auto shop used to be my go to, but not anymore. 

I recently went there because of a low coolant issue with some air in the system. I dropped off my vehicle and left it overnight. The following morning I received a call from Trung stating that I had a number of issues with my vehicle (rear main seal leak, replace oil pan, replace radiator, replace coolant reservoir, coolant flush, replace coolant hoses, etc.) The total cost for the job was well over $6,000.

This was a large bill that my wife and I discussed in detail. I decided to go back into the shop to get more clarification. Upon arrival, Thai, who I believe is the owner, fumbled around looking for my paperwork. He informed me that the quote that I received from Trung was for another vehicle similar to mine and that I needed a coolant flush, which was exactly what I had asked for in the first place. 

I paid for the coolant flush as well as the 75k maintenance package, which Thai recommended. The "work" was done the following day I picked up my car and drove home. 

While reviewing their paperwork at home, I noticed that I was charged for a new air and cabin filter. I recently replaced my own cabin filter so I had a hunch that they might not have done anything, so I checked their work. Lo and behold, it was the same exact filter I placed in. Also, I replaced my own air filter with a K&N recently as well. Most people know that K&N life time filters only need to be cleaned, not replaced. So being charged for service that didn't happen or need to happen is not right. 

I was not pleased about this and called them asking about the mistakes. Trung apologized and said he was going to refund me the amount for the parts. Rightfully so, I asked for the refund in labor costs as well since they did not do anything. Fortunately, I was able to obtain a refund. 

I went into the shop and talked to Thai about the the issues I had and asked for my refund. It took him some time but he eventually tallied up the numbers. I inquired and requested for a partial refund on the 75k maintenance cost and labor fees since the documents only indicated that an oil, and oil filter was changed. He stated that the technicians go through a list of tasks such as tire rotations, suspension adjustments, brake adjustments, etc. 

Again, I caught another inaccurate statement. My front driver side tire has a visible scratch, which I've been keenly aware of. I went to check my front tire and the scratch was still there in the same spot which means that the tires weren't rotated. Another example of being charged for service that didn't happen. 

This was a horrible experience. Lots of unnecessary stress and headache.

I definitely will not be going back here again. 

My advice, double check their work. Do your due diligence.

**Avoid Almaden Auto Repair--dishonest, overpriced, and unprofessional.** 

I brought my car in for a suspension issue (a loud creaking sound in the front end), clearly explained the problem multiple times, and even wrote it down for their reference. I was initially told my car would be finished the day after I dropped it off. While the damaged strut I mentioned was a necessary repair, it turned out not to be the cause of the creaking noise. Despite this, they performed unnecessary repairs--including brakes and a front axle seal leak--without addressing my primary concern. Based on the lengthy two-day stay and their communication, I was under the impression that these repairs would resolve the issue I so clearly outlined to them. 

On day two, I was called to pick up my car and told everything had been fixed. Within *five minutes* of driving away, I immediately noticed the creaking was still present. I returned to the shop right away and was able to recreate the issue twice in front of the employee who handled my intake. We both witnessed the loud creaking as he drove the car into the shop but still claimed the problem wasn't apparent during their inspection. After a brief review, they told me they only needed to lubricate some parts--something that should have been done during the two days they had my vehicle. However, the noise persisted. 

Upon further questioning, they finally "diagnosed" the issue as worn control arm bushings--something that should have been caught during the initial inspection, especially since the problem was clearly suspension-related. Their excuse? They didn't hear the noise during their so-called inspection. Yet now, they want to charge nearly $2,000 for additional repairs they missed the first time. 

This shop ignores customer concerns, pushes unnecessary repairs, and overcharges for subpar service. For the money and time I wasted here, they should've at least addressed the primary issue. Instead, I'm forced to find another mechanic to fix what they neglected. Save yourself the frustration--spend your hard-earned money elsewhere.

text:
Sent in my car for spark plug replacement and save the old spark plugs for me. I asked them to replace it with as specific spark plug make and model # (recommended in performance forums to increase fuel economy through more complete combustion). Also, I asked them to change out the differential oil. 

The result is that I noticed that the spark plugs they saved for me were in boxes other than the ones requested. I ask them about this and then the copped to the fact that they installed standard spark plugs not the ones I specified.

Also, I noticed that the oil they put in the differential was way way way over priced (by ~$50). I asked them about this and they said the oil was as per the Technical Service Bulletin (TSB) related to my car's make and model. I asked to read the TSB. After reading the TSB, it was apparent that they mis-read it and filled my differential with crazy expensive LSD oil in a non-LSD differential. 

So I figured these guys can't handle performance cars, can't perform services as per written customer directions and can't read TSBs. Maybe they can handle a standard car. Well, I was wrong.

Later, I sent them my wife's car. I asked them to replace the radiator hoses. 

When they completed the job, my wife noticed that there was a persistent whooshing sound coming from the engine. The car was in the shop an additional several hours before they discovered that they forgot to top off and bleed the coolant system (potential serious engine damage if not caught early).

Plus, shortly after, my wife's Credit Card (the one she used to pay for the work done) was being fraudulently used.

There are no minus stars I can award this shop. If there were, I would give them a -5.

text:
My car was leaking or losing water, I didn't know why. I brought it to the shop, told them the problem, and asked them to do a thorough check. I emphasized that I needed the car to be road-ready since I was planning to take some long trips. They called within three hours, which was nice and fast, and told me I had a leak in my water pump and it needed replacing. They quoted me $350. I was like...damn. I told them to go ahead and do it. $350 is actually very cheap. The part alone costs at least $250, and it's located inside the engine. So everything has to be taken apart just to get to it. Labor alone would be around 5-6hrs. Good deal, right? I also asked them to do a transmission flush, by the way.

Two days later, I pick up my car. Pay. They tell me everything is fine now. I should bring it back soon for a hundred thousand mile check-up. Okay, fine.

I drive for about an hour and I find my car having the same problem as before. W...T...F
What did I just pay close to $500 worth of work for? I bring it back, a day later the guy calls me and says I have a bad hose. It'll cost $80 to replace. REALLY?!?! It should be free! You replaced the wrong part! One that I didn't NEED. But oh, it's okay because he was offering a 10% discount on the labor....

When I pick up the car, he gives me the receipt. It states:
1. replaced two hoses for waterpump/engine
2. pressure check for water hose and engine
3. blah blah blah

Where was that pressure check the first time? Where was it when they decided the problem was my water pump? Where was it AFTER they installed the water pump? It was such a hassle to go back and forth when this was my ONLY car. And all that money gone for no reason. I will never go back. It makes me wonder if my water pump was even ever replaced. It's not a visible part, so I will never really know.

So here is the real problem. This place is getting so much business that they have to cut corners. They're too busy to do the little things anymore.... like appreciating the customers they have!

text:
The mechanics here are pretty good but like most places when they start getting too many reviews they start getting overwhelmed with people. 

This used to be the type of place where you're in and out. My appointment was at 9:00 in the morning, I didn't end up leaving until 4:00pm in the afternoon. And it was just for basic routine car maintenance.

I like how you can just make an appointment online. But this place just takes too much time for it to be my main main mechanic I can't afford to take the whole day off just to get an oil change.

Another thing the main guy that works there is a robot. He smiles at you and you think he's talking to you but he's actually talking in his earbuds. Even I know those people in front of you are the most important everyone else could leave a message or they can call them back.

I know at this point since they're so overwhelmed with customers they won't be able to get your car to you in a timely manner but the least they can do is let you know what's going on and how long it's going to take realistically.

I asked him if it would take an hour and he said yes but maybe he wasn't talking to me but the people in his earphones. It would be nice for them to just say hey we're really busy today can you leave your car for 8 hours.

Recommendation
1) have a sign that says SIGN CLIPBOARD AND I'll be right with you.

2) give people realistic time when they drop off their keys. For example I am going to do a diagnostic which will take 2 hours, I will need to fix A, B, C, this will take a while your car will be ready at X time. 

3) Update system where you're only doing a certain amount of cars per hour so everyone doesn't have to make this a whole day thing every time they want to get their car maintained.

We're literally have a sign when you walk in that says grab this form fill it out drop off your keys and come back in 4-5 hours.

That way people are not just waiting around not knowing what's going on. When I walked in he was too busy to even tell me to sign the clipboard clip board.
