text:
I brought in my 2007 Toyota Yaris (automatic) for squeaking brakes 06/23/2021. These were new brakes from just that past October (replaced at another shop. That is another, seperate story). I initially chose Almaden Auto Repair because they had a large number of pretty decent reviews on Yelp. 

I left my car at AAR while they inspected it and got a call later that day from an employee saying my transmission is producing a "grinding" sound and that they "didn't hear any squeaking from the brakes." Which is ridiculous because it is quite obvious of a sound and happens *every time* I brake. I have also never heard any suspicious sounds from my transmission and have had no Check Engine lights appear for any reason. I go in to hear what they are talking about and while my car is idling, I do hear a sound, though I would never describe it as grinding, it was more of a rattling sound. They claimed it was my "transmission axle bearing" which just doesn't really make sense as a description. They said that my transmission needs to be replaced and estimated me at $3600 and said it would take 2 weeks to repair. I said "No thank you", paid the diagnostic fee, and left. 

After much research online and calling other shops around for estimates, they not only weren't making sense with their description of the diagnosis (nor the description of the sound/when the sound would occur), but the consensus is that $3600 for replacing a transmission on a 2007 Toyota Yaris is INSANE. That's more than half the value of my entire CAR.

But all of this aside, I have personally found the cause of the rattling ("grinding") noise they were claiming was my transmission... My hood-stand doesn't have a proper latch and I have a short bungee cord that wraps over the top of my car battery to hold it down (Used car. Didn't come with the piece to hold my battery in place) and I tuck the hood-stand under that cord... because it *rattles* if I don't. Problem fixed and rattling completely gone.

I also feel it is worth mentioning that I am a woman. I know a fair amount about cars and tend to do my own repairs when I can. (I live in a city and don't have a garage at the moment, which is why I was looking to have it taken in.) They took advantage of that and I'm assuming they tried to scam me thinking I would accept their word as gospel. While the transmission's inner workings isn't my strongest point in my knowledge of cars, I knew enough to be incredibly suspicious of what was going on. 

TL;DR, On 06/23/2021, Almaden Auto Repair tried to pass off the sound of my hood-stand rattling on the battery as a "transmission axle bearing problem" and attempted to get me to pay $3600 (a WILDLY inflated expense) for a new transmission I absolutely didn't and do not need.

They are very fast paced and have a lot of cars at their shop, with what 2 mechanics. Felt they didn't really take the time to assess my vehicle, beware! text:
I really wanted to like this business, based on the overwhelming number of positive reviews here.

The first time I came here for my car was in June of 2013 for a 135k service. I bought the car at 105k, and was still searching for a mechanic I could trust with it. Dan was very thorough with his inspection, replacing spark plugs, the rear wheel cylinder, and the valve cover gaskets. 

He also listed his recommendations for repairs in the near future. These included A/C service, a power steering flush, a transmission flush, and rear shocks. Like I said, my car's fairly old, and while I wasn't happy about the scope of the possible repair bill, these seemed like plausible recommendations, and I decide I'd take care of those at a later date. 

We get the phone call to pick up the car because the repairs are done. 5 minutes into the drive, the "Check Engine" light comes on. I take it back to TLS, where Dan informs me that the O2 sensor had some oil drip on to it, causing it to malfunction. He tells me that the shaky condition of my car engine means that this was a fluke occurrence, and he's not responsible for it. 

I'm not happy with this outcome, and end up getting 2 other opinions; both other mechanics agree that this was unacceptable, and afterward, Dan agrees to replace the O2 sensor, at his cost. He's not happy about it, and he acts differently than when I first spoke with him. He gets a lot more terse, and when he does talk, it's with this defensive edge with things like, "This other shop didn't see [this other mechanical issue]" or "I always do [this good mechanical practice]."

Anyway, because he made good on fixing the problem, I'm satisfied. Not thrilled with his attitude, but I don't write critical Yelp reviews lightly. (Check my other reviews. I try to focus on the positive, because I know that it's hard running a small business.) Also, because things are now weird with TLS, I decide to find a different mechanic. 

So last week (early August, 2014), I end up going to a different mechanic for my 150k service. Things are mostly okay. Both the front and the rear shocks still need attention, and the valve cover gaskets are leaking again. I check my records and confirm that, huh, I got those changed 14 months and 14,000 miles ago.

I call TLS, and they say, yeah, that shouldn't be happening, and to bring the car back in so they can take care of me. 

I do that, and walk in through the door to explain the situation. 

Dan's behind the counter, and before I finish talking, he says very tersely, "Yes. I remember you." Not in a friendly way, but a way that makes me think, "Oh, man. This is gonna be awkward." 

He puts the car up on the rack, and in response to my concerns, including the valve cover gaskets and the shocks, tells me that none of them are problematic. The valve cover gaskets only look like they're leaking from the residual oil stains from how messy my engine was in the past, he says. The valve cover gaskets should last 100,000 miles, and there's nothing wrong with the ones he installed, he says. 
The shocks will eventually have to be replaced, but it's an old car, and it's heavy, and he says they're not a problem. The whole inspection takes maybe 10 minutes, tops. 

On top of it, he's still doing the weird attitude thing again. He points to the oil filter and tells me the other shop was sloppy. He quickly puts a little air in the tires and says nothing's wrong with the shocks (even though HE recommended replacing them a year ago!), but that the other shop didn't bother to put air in my tires. There's all this little passive-aggressive finger-pointing behavior that just makes me want to get out of there ASAP. 

So I nod, take the car in to a 3rd mechanic, who confirms the problems with the valve cover gaskets, and the shocks. FWIW, the other two mechanics not involved in this review have Yelp scores of 4 and 5 stars, respectively. And neither of them pulled any passive-aggressive communication with me, either.

3 stars for the first repair encounter; 1 star for the customer service; 1 star for the latest repair encounter. I'd like to give a 1.5, but because I can only give whole numbers, I'll have to round up to a 2.

***********

UPDATE: 8/9/14: 6:43 p.m. Pacific Time: 
Dan deeply cares about his Yelp reputation. Within an hour of my posting this review, he sent me a text with a copy of my invoice, and the message: "I helped you to fix the sienna at my lost and this is what i got from you....!!! WOW......." 

(Link here: http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/tls-auto-service-toyota-lexus-scion-san-jose?select=iVY1PBW4tE3gH4xFHTMZ4w#hdF8P0hgsZdFXMiZUCG7-Q)

A fact I acknowledged in my original review. 

I would also like to acknowledge that texting a customer to complain that he posted a review you don't like is deeply, profoundly unprofessional. Dan: I know you're reading this. Please don't ever contact me again. 

Revising my review to reflect this latest distasteful incident. 1 star.

replies: [{'id': 'OkeSX1iswuRV11HeOp1x6Q', 'text': "Thank you for the feedback Yu. You hired us to *diagnose* the check engine light not to fix the problem, as for fixing the problem we first have to know what the issue is before we can say we can fix it. When we ran the codes for the check engine light, you had multiple misfire codes. Every single cylinder had registered having a misfire! With only 50k miles it was too soon for spark plugs. The sensor that was in question was your mass air flow. Once we started the motor we noticed the motor was misfiring randomly. One of the first things we did was unplug the mass air flow sensor. Right after unplugging the M.A.F. the misfires went away. We have had many BMW/Mini's start running great after doing this procedure. As far as the oil being low, low or no oil would have caused permanent damage to the internals of the motor. text:
Charles is knowledgeable about cars but the price is not worth it. I requested help to look at my car that was not starting and had a coolant leak. I told him over the phone that it is probably the starter and the water pump. His charges were $50 to come out to my place and another $120 per hour. I thought that if he replaces the starter then it will be worth the trip. So I made an appointment, he showed up slightly late but I can understand there could be traffic. Looked at the car showed a trick to start the car and gave me a quote of $730+ to fix both and he told me that each requires ~1 1/2 hrs for a total of ~3 hrs. Additionally, he said that he did not have that much time that day so he will have to come back. All this he finished in ~15 mins and charged me $170. I felt ripped off to come and give me a quote of $730+ initially and then bringing it down to around $675 saying that since he did not use the complete hr he can give $60 towards the repair. 
I got the complete repair done in the shop for less than $475. So in a nutshell I got charged $170 to show the trick of starting the car with a bad started which is already available on youtube. 

The lesson learn't is before picking a mobile mechanic one needs to estimate whether the job can be finished in one hour, if not then it is just an expensive diagnosis call.

text:
My experience was uncomfortable, but it was short and tiny, and I just would like to share a complaint about their attitude. I'm just a nobody sharing my experience and never thought to get a reply that made things way worse, and later on a "compliment" from a "customer" who blamed me just because I shared this. This all sounds unbelievable to me.

My experience was very simple: I was quite urgent fixing my car, so I check their website, walked in, waited in line politely until they call me, and asked the man behind the counter if he could replace one of the struts, and if I can do walk-in, in a humble voice. He seems triggered and said that he takes appointments only, which I understood and agreed, but he still seemed to be very angry for no reason. I don't think asking if walk-in is okay to be rude. I didn't see such info on website so I decided to ask. Am I wrong?

Then he clearly misunderstood the "replace one of the struts" and mocked that "fixing one strut is like buying one shoe instead of a pair", but clearly that's not what I meant and I respect his decision as a technician. I didn't have a chance to respond since he just kept talking his own theories and supposed that I disagreed, which I clearly didn't wanna do.

I did not have any conflict or argue with this gentleman behind the counter -- our interactions in shop was very peaceful. Even I was triggered by the conversation, I just said "So you fix it or not?", after he said no I just said OK and left the shop. That was his private property, and I didn't want to disturb anyone simply because of a disagreement. I knew what I shouldn't do.

Above all was just everything about my experience. I'm just unhappy about the staff's attitude. What happened afterwards was very interesting. I left my original comment on Yelp and received a very disquieting reply from the owner. He did not show any interest in improving his communication, nor talked about any concern I had in the review, but made a worse personal accusation towards my personality while I simply told everyone what I experienced.

After 6 months, I received a "compliment" from another user who claimed to be "on scene" when I visit. This user said that "I walked in" was "very inappropriate" and "shame on me", while my total interaction with the staff was less than 10 sentences without argue, and even myself didn't quite remember what happened after this long while. Interestingly, this user also attached an AD message from this business's website.

For this "customer" if you are really one: I don't know your motivation, but appreciate you supporting your local business. However, please respect other customer's right of leaving a review, which is protected by the state and federal law. I sincerely hope you don't get "compliments" against your negative comments on other businesses like what you sent to me. Additionally, I don't know how can a few sentences without any argue sound "rude and inappropriate" to you. My visit was so short that I barely even touched any object and I didn't even have to sanitize my hands. It's either that we are not talking about the same event, or maybe you're not talking the truth for some reason.

I never thought leaving a negative review on Yelp that honestly reflects my personal experience could get me so much disturb afterwards, based on what I experienced here so far. Especially my experience itself was not a big deal -- if there was a misunderstanding let's talk it through, if I did something wrong too, maybe we can apologize to each other. However, each action I see from the owner and their "customer" made me feel uncomfortable and scared.

Everyone's time is valuable and I am not even interested in any further interaction with this business. I'll keep this review permanent from now on and will never delete it for everyone's reference. For customers who visits here, I hope you get better experience than mine -- at least it can prove that they are really improving, which I believe to be the original purpose of Yelp. 

For customers who had good experience here, I'm truly glad that you had a good experience at this shop, and it is always to hear your happy story shared here. However, please respect your peer customers' right to share feedback on any business's services, instead of sending "compliments" to argue with users just because you had a better experience. Please don't judge things that did not happen to you. Reviews only represent a user's experience -- not even a denial to anyone's personality and no need to take it super personally.

Not to mention that "shaming on" other customers is an absolute attack, and is not the way to support your local business. It only makes life worse for everyone.

on 10/24/2025 my friend took a day off from work to accompany me to the repair shop, since the shop is closed on weekends. We went there hoping to speak with the person in charge, Akin, to clarify what had happened during a previous repair.

However, upon arrival, I felt that Akin had no real intention of resolving the issue. I mentioned the Vietnamese technician who had worked on my car and asked Akin to communicate with him to understand the situation. I later learned that the technician's name is Danny. Instead of addressing the issue, Akin turned the conversation toward "racial discrimination," which was completely irrelevant and distracted from the real safety concern.

During our visit, Akin behaved in a very rude and unprofessional manner, refusing to let us speak. He simply said that my tires were new and that being over-inflated by 10 psi would not cause any problems or blowouts. However, he could not explain why the correct tire pressure should have been 38 psi, yet the technician had inflated them to 47 psi. A professional technician like Danny should never have performed such an obviously unsafe act, and it is difficult to understand why Akin would consider this acceptable.

I did not request any compensation; I only wanted the shop to take this matter seriously and prevent similar incidents from happening to other customers.

Akin also claimed he wanted to "understand my car's performance" and repeatedly started the engine to "test" the vehicle. My friend, fearing that he might damage my older car, quickly stopped him. The whole experience was very unsettling. It felt as though he was not trying to fix the problem, but rather creating new ones and revenge..

text:
I went to Akin's to repair my BWM due to his all 5 star rating. They had a diagnostic and told me two ignition coils were not working and suggested me replace all 6. I was OK and asked them to have oil change and do the regular maintenance work. I was given a quote and it looked fine to me. At the end of day I got a call and was told that the car was ready for pick-up. So far so good. The one star is for this. 

When driving the car on the way back home, I smelled something burning, but didn't think anything wrong. But after arriving home, when I parked the car, some smoking was coming out of hood. It's so terrible. I opened the hood, and found that oil was dropping onto the exhaust pipe which is very hot, what's where the smoke came from. This is a new issue, I never had this before. I thought they might just carelessly have some oil spilled out when doing the oil change. So I called Akin's next morning and they asked me to bring the car back. 

The guy who repaired my car had a quick check and tell me there are three places leaking oil. That's where the dropping come from. However what I didn't understand was why it didn't happen before. He was kind of mad and asked me to take to other dealer to have a report to prove the new oil leaking issue was caused by his repairs. I was very disappointed at his response to my question. The other guy came to explain the reason, I didn't quite understand his reasoning. Basically he meant the old oil was thicker than new oil, so no leaking was noticed before. I wasn't convinced by their explanation. They confirmed the car can be drove safely for at least another 5000 miles, so I took the car back home. 

Days after the repair, I found there are oil drops in my driving way. This was definitely a new issue since there were no oil drops on the ground before. To double confirm this, I checked my garage ground where I mostly parted my car but hadn't parked there since the repair. I didn't see any oil drops. It clearly proves that the oil leaking issue was somehow caused by this repair. I can't figure how it's caused by their repair, but they are just relevant. I'll never go to the shop again.

I cannot for the life of me fathom how this business has so many 5 star reviews, as, by my experience it's clear that Akin is a crook. 

Then again, maybe Akin was just having a bad day:

After waiting for 30 minutes in his waiting room while Akin chatted up friends, I described the problem to him with my Transmission.

Without doing a diagnostic check on the trouble light, he told me the transmission was shot and had to be replaced, to the tune of $4000 or more. 

I asked him how he could know what was wrong without at least doing a diagnostic. (I told him I suspected it was the shift solenoid, as this was a known problem on my model of car) and he only gave in after I insisted and paid his diagnosis fee. 

Afterwards, he simply said "Yeah, the trans needs to be replaced." Skeptical, I looked him in the eye and asked "Well what was the code that the test returned? What did it say?" 

He only insisted in an annoyed tone: "It said the transmission is bad and needs to be replaced, which will cost you at least $4000, and your car is not worth it." As if it was his place to decide such things.

I walked out in disgust and never returned.
However, I did order my own $30 diagnostic unit which pulled the code and confirmed my suspicions: 
The Shift Solenoid B was bad and needed replacing, not the entire transmission.

I took it to another shop, who were kind, courteous, fair and honest, and paid less than $1000 to have the problem fixed. 

The only way he has so many 5 star reviews is one or a combination of the following: 1. They're all him. 2. They're all from uneducated, unsuspected customers who don't know they've been duped and are simply happy he did a "great job". or 3. Akin is a customer of Yelp, who offer to remove bad reviews for him for a fee. (Yes, Yelp does this. I know because they contacted my own business with this offer.) 

It's sad that such a dishonest businessperson has such a great reputation on here.

My family and I used to come here for all our car needs. I had a bad experience here a year and a half ago after I had them replace my clutch, master cylinder, and slave cylinder for my G37. I took off the review because the business is their livelihood but I feel people should be aware.

When they overhauled my clutch, they didn't replace my master cylinder as agreed. Everywhere in the manual says you must replace both master and slave at the same time. I picked up the car and almost get home to find that the pedal is stuck to the floor and I can't shift. They towed it back to the shop and replaced my master cylinder and it is working again. Note that after picked up the car the second time I told them that it was driving funny. So I drove the car with Chuck in it and had him drive it but he told me it drove normal. Wouldn't I know what normal is if I am the one that's been driving it every day? I let it slide and thought it just needed to be broken in.

Just recently I was not able to get into ANY gear. I thought my clutch had worn out prematurely so I took it to another shop to get it replaced. Turns out the clutch was never adjusted correctly so I was not getting full pedal travel and the clutch was not fully disengaging. The new shop readjusted my clutch and it finally drives like how it should be.

text:
Alright, here I am posting a review to express the kindness of a mister at Leales's transmission. I pulled a transmission down from a BMW 2004 325i because it was leaking oil, I took to the auto repair, on behalf of someone suggestion. When I arrived at the place I explained that the transmission was leaking oil and that the car was making a noise under the back seat, they were very kind and helped me unloading the transmission from the trunk of my running car. 

I gave my info and was told that they were going to inspect it and let me know what was wrong, 4 hours later I got a call and was told the transmission was beyond repair/it would cost around $3500 to fix it.
So I said, I don't have that kind of money, then picked it up and BIENG HONEST THEY DID NOT CHARGE A PENNY FOR CHECKING IT. I went home and I got a call from the shop and they offered help to find a used transmission for $2000 to $3000 dollars. 

I said I didn't have that kind of money.

Long story short, my transmission was still good, i run the risk of fixing the leak and put it back on my car is running perfectly fine. 

The problem was the driveshaft, u joints were too stiff and that was causing a friction which shook the transmission multiple times and caused the seal by the oil pump and Tork convertor to loosen and leak oil. 
DO NOT ALWAYS BELIEVE WHAT YOU ARE TOLD.

So for the fact that my transmission was not inspected or it was inspected incorrectly I am giving 2 stars yelp review.

Again, the guys were very helpful, but were they truthful???

text:
This store just charge and nothing else. Problem is never solved.

Last year I took my car to them with the issue that my car overheats, they told me radiator ,thermostat have gone bad and charged me $90 for the diagnosis. Those were replaced at a cost of ~$1200 here. Few months later again the same issue happened, that time they said car was low on coolant and they refilled it, they didn't even inspect the car.Just refilled it. Problem of car over heating was never addressed.

When issue happened again as I had lil/no confidence in them I took my car to another mechanic and he told me there's an issue with the radiator and the thermostat. Similar thing was informed by another mechanic who told coolant wasn't circulating well enough, that could be due to bad thermostat or any other reason , which causes car to overheat.
And finally I took my car back to them today as both radiator and thermostat were under the warranty. They tested the radiator and thermostat and confirmed its not whats causing the car to overheat. When I asked what the issue is , they said its has to be diagnosed and would charge another $90 bucks for that. 
Isn't this exactly the same problem for which I came here before and for which I've already been charged heavily and the problem was never actually solved, then why another fees for the same diagnosis ?? I along with my friend tried best to understand why I need to pay again but failed to. The problem of overheating should have been identified when I first came to them or for that matter even on my second visit. Why shall one customer pay again for the same issue if due diligence was not done at their end.
All they could say they've verified the radiator and thermostat and that's not what's causing the issue.As professionals they are the best person to confirm which component of car is faulty which is not. For me as a driver, I only see my car is overheating, I dont' understand my radiator is at fault or my thermostat has got jammed or any other issue . That is their job to identify and fix if they do take charge of customers's trust and vehicle. 

It make no sense to be charged again and again for the diagnosis of same problem that has been plaguing since months, just becuz the parts they replaced were not faulty. What if I replace another component on their suggestion , and issue still stays, do they expect me to pay another $90 for the diagnosis as the part they replaced is not causing the issue ??? Seriously ?

They need to understand customer comes up with a problem of a vehicle as a whole and not with a problem of component.

A harassing experience it has been here.

text:
I brought my RV in for a safety inspection to the owner Fernando, on July 30, 2015 because I was going to take it on two trips soon. He agreed to inspect the vehicle and brakes for $50. After doing so the only thing he recommended was a front brake job since the brakes pads were at 15% and an oil change. He agreed to apply the inspection fee to the work and charged $350 to "Perform Front Brake Service, INCLUDING Installing New Premium Front Brake Pads" and $50 for an oil change. 

A couple of weeks after Preferred worked on the brakes of my RV. I was on the way to Monterey today when I started smelling the brakes overheating as I was driving. A short time later the brakes would pull to the left when I hit them, and the front end felt a bit jerky. I also started to notice some brake fade. I pulled over in Morgan Hill and checked under the car. Both the front brake were radiating a lot of heat, even 6 inches away. I got in and noticed the brake pedal went all the way to the floor. After the brakes cooled off for about a 1/2 hour I could get enough pressure in the brakes to carefully drive it home. 

Since I could not use the RV for the trip, I needed to get up at 4 am tomorrow to drive down to Monterey in my car since I have a job there from Friday through Sunday. 

After this trip, I dropped off the RV for three days, at the end of which he was able to duplicate the problem. When I asked if Fernando if he turned the rotors or bled the brakes, he admitted all he did for $350 was change the pads. 

At this point, he pointed out that the rotors were warped (which they were not before he worked on it, or he would have replaced them instead of just changing the pads. He gave me a quote for $2000 to fix the front brakes and change the master cylinder (which is working fine).

Since he miss-represented what he charged me for on the front brakes I brought the RV to Mission Valley Ford for an inspection since I had my next trip coming up soon. The Service Advisor for Mission Valley Ford agreed to inspect the brakes to determine what was causing the problem. The service manager called me the next day and stated that the brake pads were installed incorrectly, which caused the severe dragging and the rotor and caliper damage. He also said that the original inspection missed problems with the rear brake cylinders which could have caused them to fail. 

In addition to the $2300 incurred by Preferred's poor workmanship, I spent hours getting the brakes fixed correctly, and I had to cancel one trip. And their work could have resulted in an accident which may have led to a car crash, and worse yet bodily harm had I not canceled by trip and turned around.

Value Added Cost of going to this Service is: Engine replacement - 4K to 6K as per the Fernando, on top of the 2.2K service charge which was spent for nothing. I feel that i got robbed.

text:
I have never had a bad experience with the Yelp recommendations until this one. I was in desperate need of an oil change because I was about a month over due and having my old mechanic move out of town, I needed to find another mechanic. I went on yelp and found Thanh's Auto Service & Repair to be highly acclaimed and excitingly made my way to the Auto Shop. 

Well, it was Saturday and granted, I should have called to see if they could fit me in, but i decided to drive anyways. I made it to the shop and true to my gut feeling, Thanh said he was too busy and said to come later in the week. So I made an appointment for the following week. 

Well, I arrive at my appointment a couple of minutes late and was excited to get my oil change. Well, no one was there to receive me and one of the mechanics that didn't speak English just said to wait 5 minutes because he was on a test drive. Well, 5 minutes turned to 20 minutes. Not too bad of a wait, but seeing that I had an appointment, I was disappointed. Minus 1 Star for that. 

When Thanh came back from the test drive, I met him in the office and I told him I needed an oil change. He told me to wait outside and that he'd be 5 - 10 minutes. Well, seeing that there was no seats to wait inside, I went back to my car and waited another 20 minutes for him to even acknowledge me. Thanh then came back and told me, that it'll be 5 minutes again, and that he was going to service my car. Well, from the beginning till this point I waited around 45 minutes till he said that he was finally going to work on my car. 

Well, another 10 minutes later, he finally got my car not on the lift but under the lift and had to jack up my car to get the oil changed. Well, the oil change itself took another 20 minutes and I was expecting to get my free tire rotation (which is proudly displayed on his website) but he didn't do that also! *Another reason why I took off a star. 

Well, I was already annoyed because, I've been waiting around an hour and a half, I saw that my tires weren't rotated even though he boasts that he does it for free, and he didn't even check my tire pressure and fluid levels. *Another star taken off. 

He was gracious to take a dollar off because it took so long. And he did shake my hand and apologized for the wait. But I did make an appointment and he said I arrived 30 minutes late. I know I was 5 minutes late, but you don't argue and call your customer a liar. Overall, not satisfied at all. *Another star taken off.

text:
Based on Yelp reviews, I took my car in last February knowing it needed quite a bit of work. Having hit over 100K miles, the car needed a water pump and gasket replacement (I think, though this was -already- replaced at 70K miles), a new timing belt, power steering pump belt, alternator belt, and a few other parts replaced. My rear struts had also been leaking. Not a lot of places fix struts so this was another reason I came to Thanh's.

I know my car quite well and lately felt that something was wrong in the rear -- perhaps the brakes. My regular mechanic just told me my brake pads are fine, except that my rear struts are leaking again. I know that good struts will last you about 50K miles -- and the only driving I do is around the South Bay, mostly just to and from work (a 20 minute drive at best). 

I pulled out my old work orders and noticed that Thanh's only has a one year warranty on all of his work. I called him and explained the situation to him and he proceeded to say that it could be due to faulty struts which is not his fault, but rather the vendor's. He told me to bring the car in to assess it, and he would give me a new estimate which would likely not include the parts -- as again, he would have to discuss it with the vendor. 

Last year I paid $1,207.62 for all the repairs on my 2002 Honda Civic, which has never been in an accident ($467.39 parts, $697.00 labor, + tax). I find it questionable that the shop would use poor quality parts, which may be why his repairs are much more affordable than other shops. 

In addition, last year, Thanh told me there was a leak in my oil pan, which to this day I believe was not true and that I needed some type of Honda caps replaced that were "cracked". We have a two car tandem garage, and I'm the only one that parks in our garage. There are no oil spots on the ground where I park. In the past year also, I've taken my car to my regular mechanic as well as a Honda dealership for regular maintenance -- both of which NEVER mentioned any type of leak or parts that needed replacement. You would think the Honda dealership would try to upsell...

I would hesitate to take my car here based on my personal experience -- though the pricing for the repairs was not astronomical, I did feel that I was being duped with extraneous repairs. I'm debating whether or not I still want to take my car back in with his offer -- I'm not sure that I want his shop doing any more work on my car. That being said, because I haven't allowed him to assess the problem, am I giving this service and repair shop two stars instead of one for my negative experience -- though if he offered to fix everything, I'd definitely bump up the stars.

text:
It's official -- I was a total believer in Thanh's shop. I took my car there repeatedly for a few years while I lived nearby. Fast forward to a few months ago. I take my car in for a routine oil change and fluid flush and Thanh calls to tell me there's a problem -- I need a new clutch, so I should wait to flush out my manual transmission fluid until that's replaced so someone can do all of the work at one time. Now, my 03' Toyota has had all sorts of crazy problems, so I wasn't all that surprised about my clutch. I tell Thanh that I can't afford it now, but I'll return with the car so he can do the whole transmission/clutch at the same time. Well, we move to Santa Cruz and a month or so passes when I take my car into another Yelp favorite, a repair shop near my home. I tell the owner what Thanh told me, so he takes my car for a test drive, puts it up in the air to look at the clutch AND the fluid, and tells me that he sees no evidence that my clutch needs to be replaced (or that my fluid needs to be flushed). Not only that, but he spends AN HOUR doing these diagnostics and doesn't charge me a penny -- only a "Come back when you need an oil change!" send-off. 

Now, I know what you're thinking -- maybe it's a difference in professional opinion, right? Well, maybe. But having a clutch replaced is very expensive and a pretty significant repair, so I would have to think that it's pretty clear one way or the other if this repair needs to be done. Accordingly, I lost my faith in Thanh -- especially because, during that conversation where he made the recommendation, he said, "You know, I don't recommend things that you don't need. I'm very honest."

So, if this shop recommends a big repair, get a second opinion. It might save you a lot of money.

text:
THE GOOD:

This small shop is ran by a guy name Earl. Seems to have been in business for quite some time. I go to him on a Monday 10/20/25 for a smog diagnosis that he charged $95, about the standard price. He was able to complete the inspection and gave me a diagnosis back same day (approx. 4 hours total time). He offered a free throttle body clean because upon their inspection, the throttle was dirty and had a lot of carbon build up. I was notified the vehicle would be ready for pick up at 4:15PM, I told him I was going to be there 4:30PM. When I had arrived, earl was nice enough to wait around after they had closed for me to receive my vehicle.

THE BAD:

After I paid him for the diagnosis, he told me what was wrong and gave me the keys, then promptly left with a friend that was awaiting him. Right after I pulled off in my car, something was awfully wrong. The idle RPMS was sitting at almost 2K RPMS on a cold start and would come to about 1500-1900RPMS the entire time. As I was driving while hitting the gas you could hear what sounded like was a vacuum leak somewhere and car has some minor lost power. I call Earl immediately after, but he was already gone from the shop; Earl told me to just bring it in first thing in the morning. I bring the vehicle back to Earl on 10/21/25 a day later and present to him what had sounded like a vacuum leak. He was quick to check into but also VERY QUICK TO DENY RESPONSIBILITY. I told him that the vehicle was 110% not like this when I had brought it in and they definitely may have knocked a hose or two loose or something. 

They first told me they would not doing anything like that, and wanted to run a smoke down test in-front of me to check for vacuum leaks. I was told by Earl, they only took off the air intake boot to access the throttle body to spray carb cleaner and there's absolutely no way they caused any of the issues presented. They run the test, and there shows no leaks from the smoke. They also run a brake clean spray to see if it will choke the RPMs down (another method to check for vacuum leaks). We go for a couple of test drives back and forth, the mechanic that Earl has working for him, poor guys age is catching up to him and cannot hear a huge vacuum leak for his life.
Earl claims to hear it as well, but cannot figure out what it is. Earl first blames the brake booster, and is adamantly asserting that he or his shop did not cause this. 

***Earl THEN DISCOVERS A MISSING connection on my VSV, but the old mechanic claims it won't cause any vacuum leaks or noises and just caps it off.***. 

They then proceed to say the noise and high RPMS is an exhaust leak and show me where it is leaking. You can see exhaust smoke coming out the pipe right below the manifold but I wouldn't say it was sufficient enough to be causing such a vacuum leak noise. They adjudicate the issue is an exhaust leak, therefore, they did not cause it and cannot fix it anyways. 

It is worth mentioning I am not by any means a mechanic. I am what you call a garage monkey. I understand some concepts, but no way am I to be at the SUPPOSED level these guys are at. I have my doubts so I go home and take apart the air intake boot and further inspect the throttle body. There it is, lo and behold a vacuum line disconnected from the throttle body that was suppose to be connected the VSV. 

To summarize everything , 
Earl is a truthfully a honest guy it seems, but is seemingly incompetent on the work and guys working for him do rushed, shoddy, crude, messy work. It's not hard taking off an air intake boot and reconnecting all necessary hose lines back. Paid $95 for some problems they claim they didn't cause and don't believe the customer, ONLY to take it back home and undo the bad work they did. Crazy stuff and would not go back. Be wary of what you're doing here.

text:
The only good thing about this place is Earl can usually get you in right away. I went to him for years and had a lot replaced on a used car, and now I don't trust any of the work he did. 

I stopped going to him after having to redo a few of his repairs that were done incorrectly: one time I had a big engine oil leak after I had replaced a filter myself. I had used an aftermarket part and learned it was a bad fit. Instead of replacing the filter with an OEM one, Earl put *orange silicone* all over the aftermarket filter, and the solenoid valve it led to--all over inside my engine. And it still leaked after that! I ended up replacing the filter with OEM myself, which fixed it, and then later when I had the money took it to another shop to clean out all the orange silicone from the engine. Everyone I've mentioned this to said to never take my car back to him, so I didn't.

Ever since I bought my car, I struggled with mysterious engine problems that didn't present themselves on the test drive. It was a real pain. Later, after trying several small repairs myself and taking my car to other shops, one place found the *wrong spark plugs* were in my Honda. They were spark plugs meant for a VW or Subaru... I had had the wrong spark plugs in my car ever since I bought it, because I'd taken it straight to Earl for a tune-up. For YEARS afterward I dealt with mysterious misfiring and loss of power that resulted in a number of attempts to repair whatever was wrong, some of which I paid Earl to do! I've probably wasted thousands of dollars with this guy. The problems disappeared after the correct spark plugs were put in. 

I could tell more stories. But I think my point is made. Don't go here.

I am sad to leave a bad review, but it feels important for the benefit of the community.

Be careful.

text:
This business has changed ownership a couple of years ago and the seemingly high rating that Yelp shows mostly comes from way older reviews - take it with a grain of salt and beware because things have taken a turn for the worst lately.

I landed on this place a looooong time ago because the original owner, Roger, was a renowned Audi guy and amazing with customers. He did great work and was trustworthy so naturally, I was super pleased -- no wonder his shop had a good reputation and racked up solid reviews on here.

With that said, Carlos, the new owner/business manager, brings in an entirely different story. He incarnates that shady mechanic that we all dread.

He'll start by charging you a $150/$200 diagnostic fee before doing any actual work, even if you come prepared with specific items to get done and are not interested in anything else, or if the work is obvious or about standard maintenance.
He quoted me on a replacement part at 10x the price I eventually got elsewhere, without being able to provide a part number or even a more specific description.

I confronted him about his practices; he was prepared with explanations that barely made any sense at all. He was completely uninterested in learning and ultimately told me he did not care for my business to my face, with another patron nearby.
Cherry on the cake: I eventually got what I assume is a service automated follow-up text (I replied to warn him about this impending gloomy review) but my response got totally ignored.
This guy does not have a care in the world: he's here to make money and being a mechanic is only a facade.

Long story short: don't bother, and go next door. There are plenty of other mechanics nearby that will do a fantastic job for a much better price and without deceptive tactics.

text: I had my 2012 VW GTI towed to Berkeley Auto Service after it wouldn't start. I mentioned that the brakes had been squeaking a little, and asked them to let me know if the car was in need of anything else. Carlos got back to me the next day with a $4000 estimate that included a new fuel pump (reason the car wouldn't start), new shocks/struts (which they said were leaking), and new breaks (which they also said were leaking). Also included were new wipers ($60 for parts, and $210 for labor). I replaced the wipers myself last winter, so I know they were not needed. I also know that they take about 2 minutes to install. I called the shop and told them I was going to have my car towed somewhere else for repair. When I got to the shop, the car was running (they failed to mention this on the phone), so I drove it to a shop down the road. I shared the estimate with them, and they checked out all of the supposed issues. Turns out, the diagnoses were totally bogus! I picked my car up the next day, no repairs done, and it's been driving fine since. I understand that fuel pump issues can be intermittent, so it's possible I will encounter problems in the future, but I will not be taking it to Berkeley Auto Service when/if that's happens. My uncle, who is a mechanic, looked it up and told me it is supposed to take 0.9 hours for a qualified technician to replace a fuel pump on a 2012 GTI. They were going to charge me $420 in labor. Save yourself the trouble, find a trustworthy mechanic!

I called the owner again, to see what the problem was and brought the car back to the shop. He called me back and said he replaced the coolant temperature sensor that he replaced earlier, because its seal did not seal the coolant very well, and there's no charge for the replacement. When picking up the car, the automatic transmission stick gear switch button cover came off. I thought just popping the cover back in should be fine, and drove home. However, the coolant leak problem did not get fixed, and now the gear switch button seems to loose tension just like the door switch.

For the button problem: After the button got depressed, a lot of the times it stays depressed and never bounce back. I looked at it closely, and it is clear that it got replaced for some reason. The original button had some wears after years of depressing, such as smooth stripes on the button's surface after years rubbing with the plastic cover (yes, I did notice this detail). The "new" button doesn't have any of those wears.

For the coolant problem: Since I have some professional auto mechanic tools and Bentley manual for my car, I decided to dig to the problem myself to see what's up. It turns out that they used silicon glue to seal the plastic coolant housing with the engine block, instead of using the o-ring as printed in the manual. After I bought the o-ring from dealer for $6, putted it in and put everything back together, a lot of work, but the problem got fixed.

That's my story, and thanks for reading.

text:
Don't take your car for smog checks unless your car's computer reports 0 missing monitors.

On 10/15/20, I drove in for a smog check. It did not pass or fail. Instead, the car's on-board computer reported several monitors as not ready. I paid for the service, though the car did not pass, which I was fine with since they offered a free re-test within 30 days. I took my car home, connected my $50 OBDII analyzer tool to the car and indeed, several monitors were reporting as incomplete/not ready. As instructed, I drove the car to allow the monitors to fully test the various systems. I ended up driving 417 miles. I then plugged in my OBDII analyzer tool and noted that only one monitor reported as incomplete (INC), the EVAP monitor. My analyzer also returned a green light this time so I figured I was good to go; see images. Today, 11/13/20, with two days to spare in my 30 day re-test window, I took my car back to Quality Car Center. When I pulled up, the tech asked me if all monitors were ready. I said all but the EVAP were ready. The technician refused to test my car saying that all monitors needed to be in ready/Ok state. I was skeptical because, though my analyzer stated that the EVAP was not ready, it gave me a green light. He said I should continue to drive the car. But, I had already driven it over 400 miles. 

I took my car directly to a different Smog testing shop. I explained the situation to the tech and he said that smog shops get graded. And, by accepting a car that has the EVAP monitor in a not ready state, their grade gets negatively impacted. He admitted to not liking having to test cars such as mine because of this but that he would do it. He did and it passed. Yes, ideally, we'd all like our cars to have every monitor in a ready state, before testing, but CA does allow the EVAP monitor to be in a not ready state and still pass smog.

After that conversation, it seemed to me that Quality Car Center does not want their grade negatively impacted, so they wouldn't test my car even though they knew it would pass. They were trying to protect their grade though I had already paid them.

I drove back to Quality Car Center. All of us shared our sides; I'll admit that we argued. One of their techs even walked away during our conversation. I said that I understood their desire to protect their grade by not re-testing my car, and to make me whole, I asked for a refund. They refused. They did offer to re-test another car or get a discount on an oil change. But, that misses the point. If my car can pass smog while missing one monitor that is allowed by the state of California, why should a shop deny me a re-test after I've already paid?

While we were talking, I suggested that they connect an OBDII analyzer to each car that comes in before running smog tests and taking money. That way, they could protect their grade and the customer would not have paid anything. They said that California Smog rules don't allow that. Instead, they are supposed to connect to the car to the California Smog computer so that it can record how many monitors are/aren't ready. In the end, he said that he refused to risk his Smog certification license on just one car. If it's true, I guess California would give his shop a lower grade by testing a car with a missing EVAP monitor. Again, to protect his grade, he refused to re-test my card knowing that it would pass.

I will allow that the Quality Car Center is not entirely in the wrong... it seems that California has a share of the blame as well.... why is California negatively grading shops from testing cars that miss one allowed monitor?

In the end, my car has passed smog with the allowed missing one monitor but I've paid two shops for the privilege.

Don't take your car to Quality Car Center to get a smog check unless all your monitors are in the ready state because they want to protect their grade with California. I've pasted a link to a scanning tool below to check your monitors before going to Quality Car Center.

See research from sites below...

https://www.bar.ca.gov/Consumer/On-Board_Diagnostic_Systems.aspx
"A number of monitors are "not ready." This means the vehicle has not had the opportunity to complete one or more of the required self-diagnostic checks of the vehicle's OBD system. The number of allowed unready monitors varies by model year and fuel type."

https://antiochstarsmogcheck.com/is-my-car-ready-for-a-smog-readiness-monitors-and-drive-cycle/
"In California:
Gasoline Vehicles, 2000 and newer gas vehicles must have ALL monitors in a ready state with the exception of the EVAP monitor."

https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B01N6RKE29/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_search_asin_title?ie=UTF8&psc=1

text:
So in Jan. 2010, I brought my wife's Toyota Highlander to this shop since it was conveniently located near Santana Row and the movie theater. The car just needed an oil change and some brake work to fix the shimmy/vibration when braking. 

So I get a call from them while I'm out waiting for the car, and they tell me they're gonna need to replace the front brake pads and re-surface the rotors, which made plenty of sense since I was at 48K and the front brakes had never been serviced. What didn't make sense is they said the rear rotors needed replacing, but the the pads were fine. This is odd because usually the front brakes last about 3 times that of the rear brakes, since the front brakes do most of the work. It was strange that only the rear rotors would need replacing. I asked if they could just resurface the rear rotors, but they said there was not enough thickness left to do that. I wish I would have come back and asked to see the rotors myself. Then maybe I could have called them on their BS. 

That is not even the worst of it... Not long ago (30K miles later) I took the same car into another very reputable shop to have the brakes inspected for a shimmy/vibration. The car again needed to have the front brake pads replaced, and the rotors re-surfaced which is about normal after over 3 1/2 yrs. (30K miles later).

The CRAZY part is the shop found 1/2 the THREADS on one of the LEFT FRONT CALIPERS STRIPPED OUT WITH EPOXY HOLDING THE BOLT ONTO THE CALIPER! They had never seen anything like that before, and they noted they were surprised the epoxy held for that long. They saved the part so I could see it with my own eyes. 

So basically someone at Quality Tune-up screwed up big time, and tried to cover their mistake, creating an unsafe condition for the customer. Brake failure is no joke. Luckily for us that didn't happen. I really hope the guy who did that brake job is not working at this shop anymore. I'd strongly advise not going here for the dishonest unsafe shady work that was done on my car.
